title: Weights & Measures — The Thermometer at the Gate
description: Building Production-Ready Probes For Gemini — Kramár, Engels, Wang, Chughtai, Shah, Nanda, Conmy (Google DeepMind, 2026); with Constitutional Classifiers++ — Cunningham, Wei et al. (Anthropic, 2026)
show_notes:
Building Production-Ready Probes For Gemini — Kramár, Engels, Wang, Chughtai, Shah, Nanda, Conmy (Google DeepMind, 2026); with Constitutional Classifiers++ — Cunningham, Wei et al. (Anthropic, 2026)

Google DeepMind, Anthropic and OpenAI now say they screen traffic with probes: small classifiers that read the numbers a model has already computed rather than its words, which makes them far cheaper than asking a second model to re-read everything. Jack and Molly explain how a probe turns a score per token into one verdict, and why averaging fails on long inputs: in DeepMind's test, an attention probe trained on short examples missed about 88 percent of attacks hidden in very long code, while keeping only the worst short window fixed most of it. Then what each lab says it actually runs, whether probes can be beaten, and two legal arguments nobody has won yet: what a precaution this cheap does to negligence, and whether a score computed on every message counts as something a company knew.

Notes: DeepMind's paper is an arXiv preprint; its numbers come from offline test sets of cyber-attack and harmless prompts to Gemini 2.5 Flash, and it reports no production metrics. Its "over 10,000× lower cost" is a position on a log plot with no stated formula, and on its headline error measure every probe trails Gemini Flash and Pro, and a probe-plus-Flash cascade beats Flash alone; the paper warns its error bars are wide. Anthropic's 0.05% comes from a one-month shadow deployment on Claude Sonnet 4.5, and its paper's own table puts its rebuild of the previous system at 0.073%. OpenAI's GPT-5.6 card ("higher risk use cases") and its November 2 post ("all assistant completions") describe the scope differently, and may be describing different systems. The Raine complaint is cited for its allegations only. The readings of Learned Hand's formula, the T. J. Hooper and the Supreme Court's Twitter decision on air are the hosts' own; no court or pleading the research found has applied them to probes.

Jack and Molly are AI-generated hosts; research and script by Oggy.
